_note: Deterministic clause-risk rules used by Thoth's clause scanner. Mirrors the SOW Legal Playbook in the knowledge base (red = do not sign, amber = negotiate, green = standard). Synthetic, for demo purposes; not legal advice.

rules.why: Open-ended rework obligation with no cap.
rules.preferred: Up to two rounds of revisions per deliverable; further changes follow change control.

rules.why: Subjective acceptance standard; acceptance can be withheld indefinitely.
rules.preferred: Deliverables are accepted when they materially conform to the acceptance criteria in Appendix B; deemed accepted after 10 business days without a written notice of material non-conformity.

rules.why: Outcome guarantees (accuracy, savings) on probabilistic AI systems.
rules.preferred: Sablewood will design the service to target the agreed accuracy on the agreed evaluation set; results are measured, reported and improved, not guaranteed.
Replace with an exhaustive list; anything else is out of scope unless added by change request.

rules.why: Unbounded service with no hours, duration or SLA.
rules.preferred: Hypercare of 4 weeks after go-live, up to 40 hours, business hours; ongoing support under a separate managed-services order.
List every deliverable explicitly with its acceptance criteria.
No penalties; if required by the client, service credits capped at 5% of the phase fee and excused by client-caused delays.
Liability is limited as set out in the MSA (fees paid under this SOW in the prior 12 months).

rules.why: Assigns Sablewood's pre-existing tools and accelerators to the client.
rules.preferred: Client owns custom deliverables on payment; Sablewood retains pre-existing materials and grants a perpetual licence to use them with the deliverables.

rules.why: T&M without a not-to-exceed amount or estimate.
rules.preferred: Time and materials with an estimate of $X and a not-to-exceed amount; work beyond it requires written approval.

rules.why: Payment terms longer than the 45-day maximum.
rules.preferred: Invoices are payable within 30 days of receipt.

rules.why: Makes Sablewood responsible for parties it does not control.
rules.preferred: The Client will procure access to third-party systems and vendor cooperation; delays caused by third parties are client dependencies.

rules.why: Client obligations without a time limit.
rules.preferred: The Client will provide access within 5 business days of request; delays extend the timeline day for day.

rules.why: Response commitments outside a managed-services order.
rules.preferred: Support commitments are defined only in a managed-services order with severity definitions and business hours.

rules.pattern: terminate .*for convenience.*without payment|without payment for work
rules.why: Termination without paying for work performed.
rules.preferred: Either party may terminate for convenience with 30 days' notice; the client pays for work performed and non-cancellable costs.

rules.why: Informal change control — scope creep and revenue leakage.
rules.preferred: Changes require a written change request signed by both parties stating scope, fees and timeline impact.

rules.why: Vague data-quality assumption with no remedy.
rules.preferred: Data-quality issues found in profiling are logged; remediation beyond 16 hours is handled by change request.
